linkedin:
> It's PostgreSQL's host-based authentication file, controlling who may connect from where and how they prove it.

Per the documentation there is no fall-through: the first record matching the connection type, client address, database and user is used, and if authentication fails there, later records are not considered. So a permissive rule appended at the bottom does nothing if a stricter rule above it matched first. Order is the algorithm, not a style choice.

Read the full guide: https://www.kloudbean.com/blog/pg-hba-conf/
